results.summary: Tiny Shader v2 implements a fragment shader unit that executes a 16-instruction program per pixel to generate images and animations without a framebuffer. It outputs VGA at 640x480 (internal 80x60) and includes an SPI interface for loading new shader programs. The design is controlled via pins for pause, double instruction, half resolution, and frame/line advance. The project mimics GPU shading units and is notable for its on-the-fly color generation and SPI programmability.

This is a 3-bit flash ADC that uses seven comparators and a resistor ladder to convert an analog input voltage (0-1V) into binary and thermometer-coded digital outputs. The design is implemented with analog comparators and a resistor ladder, providing a direct conversion without a clock. It is intended for educational purposes to demonstrate flash ADC operation. The project is notable for its simple analog-to-digital conversion approach.

tt-tinytone is a PWM-based tone generator designed to drive a piezo buzzer. It uses a noise-shaping delta-sigma converter to produce a high-quality digital audio signal. The design is controlled via a simple interface and can generate various tones. It is notable for its compact implementation of audio synthesis.

This project implements a 16-bit noise-shaping delta-sigma DAC that outputs a single-bit digital signal via pulse-width modulation. The design uses a delta-sigma modulator to shape quantization noise and a PWM stage to generate the analog output. It is intended for audio applications and can be interfaced with external analog filters. The project is notable for its high-resolution digital-to-analog conversion using a simple one-bit output.

This project bridges a parallel AXI-Stream interface with a serial UART communication protocol. It converts data from the AXI-Stream bus to UART frames for transmission and vice versa. The design is useful for interfacing high-speed parallel data with serial communication links. It is notable for its role in data communication applications.

The PWM signal is generated by the temperature sensor, and this module is designed to count the number of clock cycles during which the PWM signal remains LOW. The design operates at 50 MHz and is notable for its simple PWM-to-UART conversion for temperature sensing. It measures the duty cycle of the PWM signal to determine temperature. The result is sent over a UART interface for external monitoring.

This project implements a ring oscillator circuit for clock generation. It uses a chain of inverters to produce an oscillating signal. The design is intended for use as a clock source or for characterization purposes. It is notable for its simple analog implementation.

This project implements an R-2R resistor ladder DAC that converts digital signals to analog voltages. The design uses a resistor network to produce an analog output proportional to the digital input. It is intended for analog output applications. The project is notable for its simple and accurate digital-to-analog conversion.
